testReviewTask: Audit each proposed test against its ORIGINAL requirement and assigned behavior/gapIndexes. This separate model call is self-checking, not independent validation. Exactly one decision per test. Copy the quote field of that test EXACTLY into your quote field; do not add formatting/backticks or paraphrase it. supported requires both contract-grounded assertions and coverage of the assigned behavior and all claimed gaps. Check these separately. Reject the whole proposal if ANY assertion introduces an unsupported obligation, even if other assertions are valid. Missing checks of a claimed type/behavior are insufficient coverage; missing unrelated behaviors alone do not invalidate a focused test. Inputs, API, expected values/types, exceptions and gapIndexes must be justified. An import/status-only/assert-true/self-comparison test cannot establish business behavior. A quote must contain the actual contract checked. Reject implicit preconditions, skips/xfails, monkeypatching or mocking the target. Never repair a proposal. Also return exactly one coverage review per context.coverageRuleIds entry. Compare the FULL ORIGINAL rule with the combined supported proposals and context.retainedTests, not merely the analysis gap list. complete requires checks of every explicitly stated acceptance example and equality boundary; an interior witness cannot replace a stated exact-boundary example. This is finite explicit-contract coverage, not exhaustive domain coverage. List ALL supported suite testIds for that rule, copy its full original text into quote, and quote each missing example verbatim in missingExamples. Valid focused tests stay supported even when the combined suite is incomplete. Never infer completeness from passing execution or mutation outcomes.
diagnosisTask: Diagnose every failed test in the supplied phase. Return exactly one decision for each context.failedTestIds entry, copying that ID exactly. For a generated artifact use its T ID, not its execution node or function name. Use environment only when supplied in failedTestIds. Categories: generated_test_error, requirement_ambiguity, potential_implementation_defect, environment_failure, uncertain. First locate the failing operation in the recorded traceback; then compare its expectation with the original contract. An assertion about unspecified representation or timezone identity is a generated-test error, not a defect merely because the asserted value differs. An unavailable dependency imported by the implementation before the target call is an environment_failure execution blocker. This category does not establish why the dependency is absent or prove the implementation correct; keep that root cause unresolved. A generated import that contradicts the supplied module layout is instead a generated_test_error. Use uncertain when the recorded trace cannot distinguish the blocker. Classification precedence: when a generated artifact asserts an exact outcome that the original contract does not specify, classify the unsupported assertion as generated_test_error even if the requirement is also vague; explain the ambiguity as context. requirement_ambiguity applies when competing supported interpretations prevent deciding whether the assertion is justified. Do not use uncertain merely because the reason for an already evidenced unsupported assertion is unknown. generated_test_error means an unsupported expectation or setup error in the generated artifact; potential_implementation_defect requires a justified assertion that violates a specific linked contract. An unsupported assertion is not an implementation defect. If the evidence cannot distinguish them, use uncertain. Ensure category and reason agree before returning the decision. Copy the FULL corresponding original rule text exactly into quote when an original contract applies. For environment failures without a behavior link, quote may be empty. Copy a nonempty exact substring of the failing outcome message/log into executionQuote. Logs belong in executionQuote, never in an invented evidence file. Every evidence.file must be a key in context.files and its quote an exact unformatted substring. For generated-test errors/implementation defects include BOTH source and test file evidence. Connect the failing assertion to its original expected contract. A valid failing test must be preserved. Only a generated artifact in this run can be a generated-test error. Propose NO code changes.
